messages:
jordan: heads-up — noticed p99 in the console for /v1/generate is ~420ms but the endpoint breakdown shows p99 ~1.1s for the same time window. can anyone confirm we're comparing apples-to-apples?

maria: which console widget? the route-level percentiles or the rollout aggregate?

jordan: route-level p99 (console -> Services > /v1/generate -> p99). i pulled the raw query from the console UI:

```sql
SELECT percentile(99, latency_ms) as p99, count(*)
FROM requests
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND timestamp > now() - interval '5m'
```

and it returns ~420ms. but the endpoint detail (per-client breakdown) shows a client segment with p99=1.1s and weight 35%.

sophie: are we sure the console widget is using sampled rollup vs raw per-client series? console sometimes applies route rollup that downweights small segments.

jordan: good call. i checked the query the UI runs — it hits the aggregate rollup index (rollup_window=60s). the per-client table is querying the raw ingested series. i expected them to match after rollup-blend.

rik: two likely causes: (1) rollup uses TDigest compression and we have low sample counts => merging bias at extreme quantiles, (2) per-client uses exact histogram windows which capture a heavy tail from a specific client.

maria: can you paste the per-client row? which client id is the 1.1s p99?

jordan: client_id=mobile-ios-42. per-client counts: 120 samples in 5m. overall route count 3.2k.

sophie: 120 samples is borderline for p99 stability. TDigest/decaying windows on rollup will pull the global p99 towards the larger-population clients. so console global p99 ~420ms is plausible.

jordan: but the console docs claim the route p99 is computed from the union of all samples (we thought it should reflect worst-client tail rather than population-weighted). which behavior is intended?

rik: intended behavior historically was population-weighted percentile (global view). but for SLOs we added 'cohort p99' in a different widget. maybe our docs are out-of-date.

maria: ah — product asked for a single-number SLO for route level (so product teams don't ship by chasing tiny slices). but infra folks have been asking for an option to flip to 'worst-cohort p99' for high-regulation customers.

jordan: ok—so two angles: UX should label the aggregation method. and our console query should show sampling/counts next to p-values to avoid misinterpretation.

sophie: +1. also propose we add an annotation when sample_count < 500 that p99 may be unstable.

rik: technical note: KV cache hits distort percentiles. cached requests are <50ms and massively inflate route-level p50/p95 but hide rare cold-start tails. if mobile-ios-42 hits cache less often that explains the discrepancy.

jordan: good catch — mobile-ios-42 has a different cache-key pattern (longer prompts). we see 12% cache-hit vs route average 68%.

observability-bot: deploy queued: feature/percentile-annotations -> staging at 2024-11-03T14:32:00Z :gear:

maria: for next steps: (1) change console label from "p99" -> "p99 (population-weighted rollup)"; (2) add sample_count tooltip and orange warning if samples < 500; (3) doc update explaining KV-cache skew and link to kvcache dashboard; (4) consider an opt-in "worst-cohort" aggregation in the rollout UX.

jordan: i'll file a short RFC and include example queries + mobile-ios-42 snapshot. assigning to @sophie for UI copy, @rik for metric docs.

sophie: will draft UI text and tooltip.

rik: i'll add a small note in the telemetry guide and a query to compute cohort-p99:

```sql
SELECT client_id, percentile(99, latency_ms) AS cohort_p99, count(*)
FROM requests
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND timestamp > now() - interval '30m'
GROUP BY client_id
ORDER BY cohort_p99 DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

maria: thanks — this clears it up. leaving a ticket for docs/update and tagging compliance for private deployments (they wanted worst-cohort option). :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks team. i'll post the RFC link here when ready.
